q: Which allowances on my payslip are tax free, and up to how much?
answer:
Five allowances on your payslip can be tax free. Each has a cap, and the business trip allowance has no fixed cap.

| Allowance | Tax-free cap | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Meals | 200,000 KRW a month | Only where meals in kind (e.g. a canteen) are not also provided |
| Own-car use | 200,000 KRW a month | Your own vehicle, used for work, and not alongside a per-kilometre claim for the same vehicle |
| Business trip daily allowance | "Reasonable actual cost" (no fixed cap) | Within the policy rates (20,000 KRW domestic, USD 50–80 overseas) and only for days your attendance is confirmed |
| Childcare allowance | 200,000 KRW a month | Child aged 6 or under; it stops automatically in the year the child turns 7 |
| Research allowance | 200,000 KRW a month | Qualifying roles only |

Some points that often cause surprises:

- **Going over a cap only taxes the excess.** A 250,000 KRW meal allowance taxes 50,000 KRW, not the whole amount.
- **Failing a condition makes the whole line taxable,** not just the part over the cap.
- **Trip allowance on an unconfirmed day is taxable pay.** If you also claim a meal receipt on a day you drew the trip allowance, that amount is moved back into taxable pay as double counting.

I took these from RouteMind's "Tax-free allowances and their caps" and "Tax-free allowances" documents. Both agree. I did not check your own payslip, so if a line looks wrong, the payroll desk can confirm how it was classified.
